Replay

Replay server/client runner

22 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Gameplay modelRuntime ownership and loopAdmission, delivery, and recoveryDurable authority checkpointsVerification and current limitsAuthority-side infrastructure checksPresentation failures and catch-upDelivery under transport lossOpt-in direct-host epoch discoveryPrediction limits and cooperative action timingSmall action copies under lossReceive-budget deferral

Use replay/net to run a game with an authority that accepts shared gameplay results and clients that predict local state. The runner schedules simulation steps and manages input, history, network delivery and correction. It connects a complete-world simulation to canonical codecs, transport-owned peer identities and an identity-aware presentation journal.

The API remains experimental. The sections below describe implemented contracts and their tests; the framework audit tracks broader admission, recovery and release acceptance.

Model.control_timing defaults to Scheduled. The explicit Latest_Observation profile sends one current control sample, coalesces newer producer ticks into the next authority tick, and preserves the accepted value in replay history. It has a distinct negotiated contract; the default scheduled wire/archive contract remains unchanged. Use it for external outputs such as owner-streamed physics, with game-level object/owner/sample validation. One-shot actions retain their sequenced command/outcome path.

Model.event_policy(event) -> view.Policy configures gameplay-effect timing and survives Welcome, resync and recovery journal reconstruction. Spectators remain watched; mixed presentation can delay otherwise speculative remote events. A policy set directly on a transient journal must otherwise be reinstalled after reset.

Gameplay model#

Instantiate Model(State, Control, Action, Event, Seats) and supply:

  • step(state, controls, joins, leaves, ctx): fixed-tick gameplay. Joins/leaves are bitmasks delivered exactly at their simulation tick. They are not reads of a mutable current roster during replay.
  • action(state, seat, action, ctx) -> bool: a discrete mutation over the complete world. Returning false restores all state and gameplay events produced by that action, while the rest of the tick continues.
  • control_valid, action_valid, and state_valid: the authored input/state language and invariants. The schema adds structural, finite, enum, and bit-mask validation before these callbacks.
  • hold: derive a legal held control from the previous sample. Clear transient fields here; continuous movement may remain held. Discrete commands belong in Action, not a repeated control bit.
  • neutral: a valid neutral control. user optionally points to immutable assets/configuration; it must not expose mutable external simulation state.

Simulation uses the same code on authority and predicting clients. Events still carry game-defined payloads. Source zero is reserved by the network runner for action verdicts; gameplay emits from nonzero semantic sources.

The runner supports one complete public or authored partial prediction group, one control and action type, one to eight player seats, and up to sixteen connections including observers. It refuses unscoped player prediction when the public projection omits authority-only state. Recipient views can filter snapshots, controls and events for players with validated prediction groups, or for observers. Authored group projection, footprint validation and timestamped boundary values have initial native and Claimball gates. Broader group policies remain M6 work.

On authority correction, the current full-world runner replaces older remote held-input guesses in the replayed suffix using the snapshot's held-input boundary. It applies hold once per prediction tick, including bootstrap and continuation, while preserving this client's recorded controls, aiming stamps and action IDs. For a scoped group, remote control slots are neutral and outside simulation members are removed by the authored projection. Boundary coupling is explicit.

client.correction reports the latest successful correction with before/after frames at the same prediction tick, a serial, authority tick and replayed-tick count. Read it after each pump (after session_frame in the Godot facade); copies are detached values. It resets on Welcome. A view can pass matching positions to view.smooth_correct without treating ordinary forward motion as correction. Storing the report costs two additional world values per client; large runtime owners should use stable heap addresses. Further storage/copy optimization remains subject to the roadmap's workload measurements.

An optional profiling clock records replay wall time/depth and histogram bounds without entering simulation or the network contract. Godot Sessions install it automatically.

A complete snapshot ahead of a briefly stalled client can be adopted directly when all intervening authoritative facts remain available. The runner preserves the journal and action queues, reprojects the group and rebuilds bounded prediction lead. Stats.snapshot_catchups records this path; it does not require a full Welcome/resync round trip. Godot drops the already-accounted-for frame backlog. Actual history/fact exhaustion still resyncs. client.resync_notice records the reason and relevant tick frontiers for diagnosis; view_reset also changes on a snapshot catch-up so consumers can cut obsolete smoothing.

Runtime ownership and loop#

Server(...) and Client(...) own timelines, schemas, queues, and histories. Keep them at stable addresses and destroy them once. Their transports are borrowed: destroy the runner before closing the transport adapter. The immutable model is passed into core stepping via Step.user; it is not part of frame state.

On the authority:

  1. server_init supplies the initial frame and model. A nonzero local_seat creates a listen-host player; zero is a dedicated authority.
  2. Call server_pump(now_ms) each render/service frame.
  3. For fixed simulation ticks, set local controls if applicable, then call server_step. server_issue queues the host player's discrete action.
  4. Read the current frame and emitted events for local presentation.

On a client:

  1. client_init supplies the same model/content contract, authority connection, and a stable opaque token. spectator = true allocates no player seat.
  2. Call client_pump(now_ms) to admit, receive facts/snapshots, reconcile, and maintain connection liveness.
  3. Once running, client_step(control) predicts one fixed tick. The exposed clock_scale nudges the local clock to maintain input lead. Initial lead uses the measured welcome round trip with a configured floor and bounded ceiling.
  4. client_issue(action) returns a sequence ID for an action predicted at an upcoming tick and delivered reliably. Drain authoritative results through client_outcomes and presentation changes through the client's journal.
  5. Use client_observed for authoritative sparse frame pairs on the watch clock; predicted old frames are not remote observed truth.

Admission, delivery, and recovery#

Snapshot acknowledgments are unreliable latest-state reports regardless of the logical snapshot size or its delivery channel. New snapshot receipts and the existing periodic heartbeat path resend the latest validated ID/hash. A lost ACK can postpone baseline advancement, but cannot hold later actions behind its retransmission in an ordered reliable stream. The authority ignores older IDs and requires a retained matching snapshot hash and current binding before advancing. Large bootstrap snapshots still wait for a valid ACK; periodic resend releases that gate after loss. Baseline-miss requests and gameplay action delivery retain their existing reliability policy.

  • The handshake checks schema/protocol and content contracts. A connection cannot occupy multiple seats, and an already active token cannot be taken over by a different connection. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests on the server.
  • Tokens are bearer reconnect credentials, not account authentication or transport encryption. Supply unpredictable tokens and the appropriate transport/deployment policy. The Godot sample uses random tokens normally and deterministic labels only for tests. session_profile from replay/godot/storage persists a local credential separately from the checkpoint's roster of token hashes.
  • A stable seat is reserved across disconnect/reconnect. This initial version reserves seats until explicit release. server_set_locked, custom admission, kick, ban/unban, and server_release_seat supply basic room controls. Release requires a disconnected seat with settled actions and a model reset_player callback; initialization for the next occupant occurs inside its joining tick. Bans survive reservation release and durable checkpoint recovery. Custom admission policy bytes and a policy ID can be archived; the application must reinstall the corresponding callback when restoring.
  • Input windows contain eight tick-stamped controls. The entire window validates before buffer mutation. Sender connection plus connection generation chooses the seat; packet data cannot select another player. The first valid value for a tick wins, and old/far-future inputs cannot rewrite authority history.
  • Actions are reliable, ordered by sequence, and deduplicated. They execute in stable seat order. Stale/far-future/invalid actions receive explicit verdicts; ordinary game rejection reports Predicate. Recent results and both received and settled frontiers survive reconnection so new actions cannot reuse an unresolved sequence.
  • Complete occurrence batches use the reliable channel. State snapshots use the unreliable channel and supersede older pending snapshots. Correction waits for matching occurrence history, settles the authoritative prefix, and reconciles the speculative suffix.
  • Prediction stops at a bounded horizon. Missing history or a long blackout enters explicit resync and requests a fresh checkpoint. Connection generations and checkpoint serials fence delayed input/snapshot traffic. Outstanding action IDs are preserved or settled explicitly.
  • Per-pump byte/packet caps and per-seated-peer token buckets bound ingress work. Fixed queue/history limits return backpressure or recovery states. Consumers must drain presentation and action results regularly.

Durable authority checkpoints#

checkpoint_capture, checkpoint_encode, and checkpoint_decode produce a versioned complete authority archive. server_restore starts a fresh runtime at its exact frame under an explicitly newer epoch. It preserves roster reservations, token hashes, room locks/bans, action received/settled frontiers and recent results, and pending simulation decisions. The caller chooses whether queued actions are preserved or explicitly retired. The archive uses authority projection and is limited to 1 MiB; it must not be sent as an ordinary public snapshot.

Low-level listen hosts must call server_set_local_token before capture. The Godot Session does this during opening. Checkpoint owns its arrays; keep it by pointer, destroy it once, and never copy a live owner. Decode requires an empty destination and expected content ID, and validates before installing any data. Runtime callbacks, connections, snapshot caches, presentation journals, and live allocators are rebuilt. Recovery contract specifies the format, policies, verified guarantees, and remaining migration work.

For repeated archives, initialize a Checkpoint_Codec with the state/control/ action/event types and seat count, then pass it as codec to encode/decode. Destroy it once with checkpoint_codec_destroy. It retains schema programs, not game state. Every call still validates content, policy, values, and runtime contract; using a cache for a different type set is rejected. The uncached convenience path remains available and emits identical bytes. Recovery receivers and Link keep these programs warm automatically.

client_authority transitions a surviving client to an approved newer epoch. Its Welcome resolves pending old IDs against the recovered frontiers, restarts sequence allocation from the ledger, and resets prediction/presentation. Consume client_recovery for Applied/Rejected/Retained/Retired/Settled_Unknown decisions. Unknown or lost work is explicit, and already accepted IDs are not awarded twice. See the Room driver for the integrated lifecycle and limits.

Verification and current limits#

Shell
nix develop --command bash tests/replay_net/run.sh
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_hello/network_run.sh

The engine-free suite covers join/movement/observer convergence, contested action prediction, rollback of failed mutations, loss/jitter/duplication, blackout resync, stable-seat reconnect, contract/token rejection, action deduplication, and forged sender or malformed input-window rejection. Checkpoint tests cover complete private state, promotion, pending-action policies, malformed archives, policy restoration, new-epoch fencing, and fresh-process-style stable-seat reconstruction. It also type-checks the instantiated runner for WASM.

The Godot gate uses four real processes: a dedicated authority, two predicting players, and an observer. Every process has 120 ms injected receive delay by default (about 240 ms round trip). Players move immediately, reliable firing actions settle once, and every participant observes the authoritative shots.

Snapshots now use acknowledged canonical baselines and sparse XOR deltas, with full fallback for dense changes or missing baselines. snapshot_history bounds the cache; delta_snapshots=false selects a full-snapshot reference mode. ACKs must match actual sent IDs/hashes within the current connection/checkpoint context. Facts encode only active occurrences, so empty ticks have a small header.

egress_bytes_per_second and egress_bytes_per_pump bound outbound traffic. Peer iteration rotates; checkpoints/facts precede optional snapshots. Per-peer burst credit is capped at a quarter-second of the configured rate or one complete protocol packet, whichever is larger; see delivery under transport loss. Deferral retains reliable work and lets newer state supersede unsent snapshots. Stats expose full/delta counts, saved bytes, baseline misses, rejected ACKs, and egress deferral. The protocol contract is now version 7, including compact scheduled-input windows, removal, fresh-seat semantics, required permits, process incarnation in Hello, and input-bound aiming context. Archive format 4 preserves validated held/future view contexts, incarnation metadata and the permit requirement. Room's identity check binds the incarnation to the coordinator-provisioned game-token hash before admitting traffic. Protocol-6 peers and archives require explicit conversion/update; this experimental version does not silently reinterpret them. Compact input framing changes bandwidth, not input timing or the eight-sample recovery window. Snapshots larger than unreliable_packet_limit (1,200 bytes by default) use reliable delivery so large full snapshots do not depend on lossy UDP fragmentation. Small deltas continue to use the superseding unreliable path. Each peer has at most one unacknowledged large snapshot; new large snapshots wait for its acknowledgement. Facts and small deltas may continue. Large snapshots use the same unreliable latest-state ACKs as smaller snapshots, with the periodic heartbeat ACK as a fallback. A validated baseline miss releases the gate so an undecodable in-flight delta cannot prevent a replacement full state. This bounds ordered state backlog during bootstrap and on slow connections; large-state update frequency is consequently limited by acknowledgement latency.

Failure-corpus expansion and admission/recovery review remain required. These tests do not establish host migration, owner-streamed co-op, deterministic P2P, browser runtime behavior, arbitrary scale, or parity with the full comparison games.

Authority-side infrastructure checks#

Model.action_admit(user, seat, action) is optional and runs only at authority admission, after static action/time checks and sequence deduplication. Its separate action_admission_user may query local infrastructure, such as validated asset availability. Keep the query local and nonblocking; a permit is checked again before queue mutation. Rejection is recorded as Invalid in the normal action verdict ledger. Prediction, simulation replay and audit use that recorded decision and never call the infrastructure hook. Model.user remains immutable simulation configuration. Reinstall the correct model when resuming a runtime; callbacks and pointers are not checkpoint data.

Runner timing diagnostics separate ordinary advances, snapshot processing and correction/replay, with optional bounded raw-sample consumers.

Correction selection retains the tick associated with each canonical snapshot cache entry. When the newest snapshot is ahead of contiguous reliable facts, the client can apply the newest older cached snapshot whose facts are complete. This prevents a continuously advancing unreliable snapshot stream from starving correction until the prediction horizon is exhausted. Cache/history bounds still apply. The first snapshot awaiting facts also remains in the pending slot even if newer snapshots wrap the delta cache. This does not approximate missing facts or reconstruct evicted state.

client_outcomes optionally reports which queued verdicts were recovered through a Welcome/journal reset. The Godot Session facade presents those as confirmed action-result changes, so a stale/future action verdict survives a full resync. Ordinary fact-delivered results retain their existing presentation route.

A same-epoch Welcome rebases the existing presentation journal. Queued changes survive, already confirmed watched effects mature at the new checkpoint, and abandoned speculative effects receive cancellations. The runner checks output capacity before installing the checkpoint; a full queue defers installation until the consumer drains and the normal Resync request retries. Only newly recovered Welcome verdicts use Session's synthetic route, avoiding duplicate confirmed verdicts. First admission and authorized epoch changes retain their distinct initialization/reset behavior. Unknown effects in missing history are not invented; this preserves known obligations, not a complete effect log across arbitrary gaps.

Scheduled clients refine their welcome-time prediction lead from acknowledged-input turnaround and arrival margin. Local send history is bounded, stale samples are rejected, and large excess lead can drain without retiming queued controls/actions. The existing clock_scale contract remains the integration point; Godot Session applies it automatically.

Presentation failures and catch-up#

On Error.Presentation, Client.presentation_failure records the last failed journal operation: predicted or authority batch, confirmation, or watched-clock advance. It includes the journal's specific error, requested tick, confirmed/watch frontiers, prediction head, queue count and occupied ring slot, with a serial that increments on failure. It contains no gameplay payloads, is local to the client, and is cleared on client destruction. A zero serial means no runner journal failure was recorded; an adapter can also report undrained presentation output.

After an ahead snapshot, the pump confirms its retained facts and advances the watched clock before rebuilding prediction lead. This permits old watched effects to finish before the prediction ring reuses their storage. No history, output capacity, event identity or timing policy is relaxed. Consumers must still drain the journal after pumping/stepping; the diagnostic record is not error recovery.

A receive batch may itself span more than the fact ring, even when the transport retained complete snapshots and every needed event. Before an incoming valid fact would overflow that ring, the receiver tries to apply a usable retained snapshot, mature its watched effects and rebuild prediction lead. This can release an older complete prefix even when a later fact is still delayed. Mid-batch work uses zero elapsed presentation time; the pump advances that clock once at its end. If no usable snapshot can release space, the existing Facts_Overflow resync still applies. Journal output capacity and packet/byte budgets are unchanged. See the receive-backlog regression.

Large snapshots can use negotiated unreliable parts, with bounded send/reassembly storage and existing canonical validation. Bootstrap, facts and the fallback for pre-extension protocol-7 peers retain their delivery rules. More frequent received worlds can increase bandwidth and correction cost; measure freshness and cost together.

Delivery under transport loss#

Capable peers can use two-erasure snapshot parity to complete a fragmented snapshot despite two missing shards per group. The receiver still verifies the complete digest and canonical state. Extra parity shares the existing egress budget; it can improve delivery under loss while reducing send cadence. The extension is negotiated, bounded and locally optional.

Per-peer burst credit is bounded to one quarter-second at the configured rate, or one complete protocol packet when larger. This permits bootstrap without banking seconds of traffic for a catch-up burst. Existing steady byte budgets remain in force.

Peers can negotiate compact recent facts, sharing packet headers while retaining every occurrence and the same delivery cadence. Older peers retain the original bundle format.

Up to four recent facts may also be bundled onto the unreliable channel every other authority tick after capability negotiation. The bundle fits the smaller of the configured unreliable limit and 1,024 bytes. The original reliable stream remains the guarantee; copies use normal budgets and exact-tick deduplication. Facts that do not fit are excluded. Bundling avoids consuming one RTC credit per copied fact. The complete bundle is validated before any contained fact commits. Stats.redundant_facts and redundant_fact_bytes expose that extra traffic. It can shorten a retransmission gap but is not a congestion-control or loss-free-delivery guarantee.

Peers that also negotiate fact repair (feature bit 8) request up to four missing facts in a 32-tick window, at most once per 100 ms. The server confirms support before requests begin. Each reply is an ordinary, independently validated Facts packet on the unreliable channel; filtering uses the requested historical frame and recipient. The reliable stream remains active. Missing requests/replies are retried while a validated authority tick proves the gap exists. Duplicate requests share the server's per-peer 100 ms limit and normal receive/egress budgets.

Replies must fit the negotiated unreliable packet limit (at most 1,024 bytes). Oversized facts wait for the reliable stream; this extension does not fragment facts, guarantee a maximum stall, or recover history that has expired. Binding, Welcome serial, epoch and content checks fence old requests/replies. Negotiation and retry state reset at each Welcome; base contract and checkpoint formats stay unchanged. Set client.fact_repair_enabled=false before its first pump to disable this extension. Stats.fact_repair_requests, fact_repairs, fact_repair_bytes and fact_repair_oversize expose requests, accepted reply traffic and size fallback.

Before any scheduled input has been acknowledged, clock feedback gently increases prediction lead within the configured bounds. Otherwise a client whose initial inputs all arrive stale has no echo from which to calibrate and can remain stuck. Once an echo arrives, normal arrival-margin discipline resumes. No queued action or input is retimed.

Per-peer rate admission reserves 32 additional bytes per logical packet as modest framing/retry headroom. Counters remain actual accepted application bytes; the per-pump buffer budget also remains in application bytes so one maximum packet can fit. This allowance is not a measurement of every backend's wire overhead.

Opt-in direct-host epoch discovery#

A fresh direct client may call client_discover_epoch(client, nonce) before its first Hello. The nonce must be a fresh, nonzero 16-byte challenge, distinct from its reconnect token. An unleased host opts in with server.epoch_discovery=true. The query contains that challenge and the existing game contract; the reply echoes both under the host's current epoch. The client requires the selected transport peer, matching content/contract/challenge, a valid envelope and no installed world. Only then does it send the ordinary epoch-scoped Hello with its reconnect token. The query itself carries no credential and reserves no peer/seat.

This is an optional protocol-7 extension (kinds 20/21), outside the base contract and checkpoint format. Existing explicit-epoch peers retain their handshake. Discovery requires both endpoints to support/enable it. Unsupported or disabled endpoints time out; the client does not fall back to a guessed epoch or older protocol. Retry uses the existing 500 ms joining cadence and timeout; server ingress/egress budgets still apply. After discovery, subsequent replies cannot change the client's epoch. Running/resyncing clients must use the explicit recovery APIs for authority replacement.

This query trusts the endpoint already selected by the application/transport. It is not endpoint authentication, election or a substitute for a coordinator grant. Permit-controlled clients cannot enable it, and leased servers never answer it. The Godot Session_Options.discover_epoch convenience option applies those rules and generates a fresh challenge; it defaults off. Speedball enables it for direct sessions so Join/Watch works after a manual save/resume without exposing epochs in the game UI. See the save/discovery result.

Prediction limits and cooperative action timing#

Reaching max_prediction returns Capacity from client_step and increments Stats.stalls while preserving the readable world, journal and queued actions. Continue pumping. An ordinary correction or complete ahead snapshot can resume prediction using retained facts; actual fact/history exhaustion still requests a resync. A stalled prediction is not a fresh authority observation. Monitor both stall attempts and received-frame progress when assessing responsiveness.

Model.action_timing defaults to Scheduled: requests target their proposed simulation tick and stale/future requests are rejected. Receipt is an explicit cooperative policy that queues a valid request for the next available authority tick, preserving per-seat FIFO order. The client's proposed tick does not choose the authority's execution time in that policy. Payload validation, admission, sequence deduplication, capacity limits, gameplay predicates and atomic failure remain unchanged. A request arriving during a cooldown may still be rejected by the game predicate; receipt scheduling is not an automatic gameplay retry.

Clients continue predicting actions locally. Their predicted execution time/state may differ from the authority's actual receipt-time result, so normal corrections and event cancellation/confirmation still apply. Use confirmed presentation for effects that must not occur speculatively. client_outcomes reports the actual settled result once per sequence; receipt policy does not change control timing or historical-query validation.

For a game with both delivery requirements, set a versioned per-action classifier:

Odin
model.action_schedule = {
    id = 0x4d5947414d450001,
    timing = proc(a: Action) -> net.Action_Timing {
        return a.kind == .Dash || a.kind == .Interact ? .Receipt : .Scheduled
    },
}

The callback overrides action_timing for validated payloads. It must be pure and depend only on the action and immutable rules. A nonzero ID and callback must be provided together; change the ID when the classification changes. The ID joins the negotiated/checkpoint contract, so a peer with a different policy cannot silently connect or restore. An unset classifier preserves existing contracts and wire/archive layouts. Invalid timing values are rejected before admission.

Both kinds share the bounded per-seat FIFO and sequence/outcome stream. A future scheduled action can therefore delay a later receipt-time action; the classifier does not create a second priority queue. Only receipt-time payloads may be newly queued during same-epoch resync. The authority records admission ticks and reasons; correction, checkpoint restore and explicit checkpoint conversion preserve those decisions without calling the classifier again. Host-local actions are already at the authority and use its next available tick.

Short button presses that require a delivery verdict belong in actions. Capturing a scheduled control only establishes local sampling: retransmission can still arrive after that tick. Receipt scheduling avoids that deadline, while gameplay predicates can still reject an intent, such as a dash during cooldown. Consume a latched intent after successful queue admission and handle its settled outcome.

The action policy is part of the negotiated contract and checkpoint contract. Scheduled mode preserves its existing contract bytes. Mismatched action policies cannot join or restore a checkpoint silently. Checkpoint conversions compute the target model's contract explicitly; already-admitted pending actions retain their recorded authority schedule. The isolated endurance comparison opts into Receipt; existing game projects keep their configured policy.

Scheduled input sampling also waits when its next tick is at or behind validated authority progress. client.authority_tick_seen tracks accepted snapshot, scoped snapshot-part and fact progress even while missing facts prevent installing that snapshot. A small old correction must not free one obsolete input step and consume a new press just before a complete newer snapshot catches the client up. This retains pending input at the caller; it does not retime an already-captured sample or make an unreliable input stream infallible. Latest-observation controls retain their separate receipt-time semantics. Welcome resets the frontier to its new scope.

Receipt-time clients may enqueue validated actions during a same-epoch Resyncing phase when their player identity and prior binding are already established. The existing bounded action queue owns them; no packet is sent and no prediction runs until a new Welcome installs the binding. Original sequence IDs remain, prior outcomes settle normally, and queued requests are then sent through the ordinary receipt/admission path. This is queue admission, not an authority verdict. Scheduled-action clients, joining/migrating clients, spectators, terminal phases, invalid payloads and fenced permits keep their existing rejection rules. Capacity and timestamp-overflow checks still apply. A later disconnect can leave an unsubmitted intent unresolved; this is not durable input logging or guaranteed execution after an arbitrary process crash.

Small action copies under loss#

Periodic heartbeats use unreliable delivery. They refresh liveness for the current binding and are repeated every 500 ms; they have no ordering dependency with later actions. The existing timeout and other validated-traffic liveness rules remain.

Capable peers negotiate recent action bundles (feature value 64, kind 25). The server confirms that capability before the client sends a bundle. The reliable submission and 500 ms retry path stay active. A client additionally copies up to four oldest contiguous, already-sent requests at most once per 100 ms. The bundle fits the configured unreliable limit capped at 1,024 bytes. Large actions retain reliable-only delivery; the framework does not fragment these copies.

Every enclosed request retains its original generation, Welcome serial, sequence, prediction tick and value. Copies neither retime nor predict an action again. The receiver validates the entire bundle before processing its prefix, then uses the ordinary admission, timing, ordering, deduplication and verdict path. Each inner action consumes a packet credit; all actual bytes consume the existing receive byte budget. This does not bypass authority admission or make stale scheduled commands valid. Missing/reordered copies are retried while requests remain pending; the reliable stream remains the delivery guarantee.

The bundle uses the generation/serial/count header already used by recent facts, with a distinct message kind and independently enveloped canonical Action packets. No base contract or checkpoint format changes. Welcome resets negotiation and copy timing. Set Client.action_copies_enabled=false before first pump, or Session_Options.disable_action_copies=true, to opt out. Scrapyard exposes RSY_ACTION_COPIES=0 (browser query action_copies=0). Counters are action_copy_batches, action_copies, action_copy_bytes and action_copy_oversize. Extra copies cost bandwidth and do not guarantee a fixed latency bound during arbitrary loss or congestion.

Receive-budget deferral#

Receive budgets preserve packets: pumps supply the remaining byte allowance to the transport and stop on Buffer_Too_Small, leaving the packet queued for the next pump. Crossing the budget no longer discards reliable facts or actions. Existing packet/byte limits and transport storage bounds remain intact.

Latest-observation clients negotiate packet-local sparse observations when both peers support them. Canonical values, cadence, admission and checkpoint contracts stay unchanged; old peers and dense values use the full packet.
